question: Goldbach’s conjecture states that every even integer greater than \(2\) can be written as the sum of two prime numbers (for example, \(2016=13+2003\)). So far, no one has been able to prove that the conjecture is true, and no one has found a counterexample to show that the conjecture is false. What would a counterexample consist of?
solution: The conjecture says that every even integer greater than \(2\) has a representation as a sum of two primes. To disprove it, one would need an even integer greater than \(2\) for which no such representation exists. Odd integers are outside the claim, and a decomposition into nonprimes does not rule out a different decomposition into primes. Thus a counterexample would be an even integer greater than \(2\) that cannot be written as the sum of two prime numbers, choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
